Native attack/target panel: reconstructed control flow from the installed AMD64 PE images

Images come from data/runtime/native-pe-images.json:
  reference: Steam 53.16 Dwarf Fortress.exe
  classic: official 53.16 Dwarf Fortress.exe
  Both use image base 0x140000000. Addresses below are RVAs.
  The complete renderer machine code is retained in reference-render.asm and classic-render.asm.
  These are source extraction files. No desktop or game control is used.

Renderer
  reference [0x878600,0x880118), classic [0x875e80,0x87d998).
  screen = RCX; screen.stage = *(int*)(screen+4).
  Bounds helper 0x872d70 fills L,R,T,B. It contains no user-visible text.
  Classic instruction RVAs in this renderer are reference RVAs - 0x2780.
  Reference heading dispatch table 0x880044 and content dispatch table 0x88006c:
    stage  heading entry  content entry  meaning
    0      0x87889d     0x878c3b      choose target
    1      0x87890b     0x879261      confirm attack/conflict
    2      0x878acf     0x87949c      choose Strike/Wrestle/Parry/Block/Dodge
    3      0x878af5     0x879f78      choose target body part
    4      0x878b22     0x87a8c2      choose attack, inspect speed/hit quality and attack styles
    5      0x878acf     0x87949c      choose parrying weapon
    6      0x878acf     0x87949c      choose blocking item
    7      0x878acf     0x87949c      choose dodge direction
    8      0x878bb6     0x87cb4d      wrestling relationship/action records
    9      0x878bb6     0x87cb4d      wrestling relationship/action records
  Values >9 go directly to the epilogue; no caption is generated.

Reconstructed main renderer
  draw_outer_rectangle(L,T,R,B);
  if (stage != 1) {
      draw_done_button(R-8,T+1,width=8,height=3);
      draw_text(R-6,T+2,"Done");                // 0x87881e, draw 0x87883c
  }
  heading_position = (L+2,T+2);
  switch(stage) {
    case 0:
      if (screen[0x31d] && !screen[0x31c]) text("Who will you wrestle?");
      else text("Who will you attack?");
      break;
    case 1:
      target = screen.target_at_0x30;
      if (target.flags_0x118 & 0x400000)
        text(unit_identity(target) + " has yielded.  Attack anyway?");
      else if (conflict_lookup(controlled_unit,target) == -1)
        text("Really start a conflict with " + unit_identity(target) + "?");
      else text("Really attack " + unit_identity(target) + "?");
      break;
    case 2: case 5: case 6: case 7:
      // 0x878acf calls 0x872f10 using bounds L+2,R-10,T+2.
      target_summary(screen.target_at_0x38,L+2,R-10,T+2);
      // No "Who will you attack?" title exists in these stages.
      break;
    case 3: text("What do you want to aim for?"); break;
    case 4:
      text("Attack " + bodypart_name(screen.target_at_0x38,screen.bodyparts_0x100[selected]) + ":");
      // bodypart getter 0x13345d0 at 0x878b71.
      break;
    case 8: case 9:
      text("Wrestle " + capitalize(unit_reference(screen.target_at_0x38)));
      // unit reference 0x1331500 at 0x878bd9, capitalize 0x52d3c0.
      break;
  }
  switch(stage) {
    case 0:
      list_at(L+1,T+4) with record_height=8;
      for every visible candidate in screen.vector_0x10:
        draw_rectangle(record width = available panel width, height=8);
        draw_portrait_or_classic_unit_symbol(L+1,y, width=12);
        draw_hotkey(L+14,y+1);
        draw_text(L+16,y+1,unit_identity(candidate));
        for action in candidate.action_vector_0x7d0:
          if (action.kind!=-1 && y<record_y+8) draw_status(L+19,y++,action,candidate);
      break;
    case 1:
      draw_rectangle(gps.button_horizontal_option_active,L+2,B-3,L+12,B-1);
      draw_text(L+4,B-2,"Confirm"); draw_hotkey(L+4,B-1,0x15b);
      draw_rectangle(gps.button_horizontal_option_remove,R-11,B-3,R-2,B-1);
      draw_text(R-9,B-2,"Cancel"); draw_hotkey(R-9,B-1,5);
      break;
    case 2: case 5: case 6: case 7:
      list_first_y = T+13; row_height=3;
      draw_hotkey(L+1,row_top+1); draw_text(L+3,row_top+1,caption);
      stage 2 uses screen.vector_0xd8 values:
        0 -> "Strike";
        1 -> "Wrestle";
        2 -> "Parry (" + rating(max_parry_level(controlled_unit)) + ")";
        3 -> "Block (" + rating(skill_level(controlled_unit,44)) + ")";
        4 -> "Dodge (" + rating(skill_level(controlled_unit,103)) + ")";
        others -> empty native caption;
      max_parry_level:
        foreach weapon in screen.vector_0x40:
          max(max_parry_level, max(weapon_skill(controlled_unit,weapon), skill_level(controlled_unit,97)/4));
      stage 5:
        attack = item designation of incoming attacking item + optional RAW sub-attack + RAW attack name;
        if incoming item absent, attack = attacker body part name;
        caption = "Parry " + attack + " with " + item_designation(selected_parrying_weapon)
                   + " (" + rating(max(weapon_skill, fighter_level/4)) + ")";
      stage 6:
        attack assembled as for stage 5;
        caption = "Block " + attack + " with " + item_designation(selected_blocking_item)
                   + " (" + rating(skill_level(controlled_unit,44)) + ")";
      // If attacking item resolves to null, attack may be empty and the source has two spaces before "with".
      stage 7:
        caption = "Dodge " + direction_to(controlled_unit,screen.dodge_xz[index],screen.dodge_y[index]);
        // direction helper 0x74f220, literal and branch extraction in helper files.
      break;
    case 3:
      list rows height=3; body-part field at L+7, hit-quality field at L+45;
      bodypart_name(target,entry.part_id) draws with a 36-column native cap;
      chance = entry.chance - ((entry.flags & 0x8000) ? 1 : 0);
      text(chance<=-3 ? "Impossible strike" : chance==-2 ? "Difficult strike"
          : chance==-1 ? "Tricky strike" : chance==0 ? "Normal strike"
          : chance==1 ? "Easy strike" : chance==2 ? "Easier strike" : "Simple strike");
      text(", "); text(contact_quality(entry.contact));
      draw_independent_advantage_marks(entry.flags); // +,+,-,-,!; they are not skill/rating text.
      break;
    case 4:
      attack label = weapon-RAW attack / optional sub-attack / full item designation;
      if unarmed:
        label = bodypart-RAW attack + optional '/' + bodypart_name(controlled_unit,first associated part);
        if no associated bodypart: label = "push";
      // RAW attack names remain data, not a finite hardcoded English noun list.
      // Specific comparisons stab/slash/slap/hack/bash/lash/pommel/punch/kick/bite/sting/snatch
      // select artwork; the visible label still comes from RAW strings.
      label draws from L+7 with native cap 36; summary starts at L+45 on the same text baseline.
      // Normal is omitted when speed_class != 3; the speed starts the caption instead.
      text(chance<=-3 ? "Impossible" : chance==-2 ? "Difficult" : chance==-1 ? "Tricky"
          : chance==0 ? (speed_class==3 ? "Normal" : "")
          : chance==1 ? "Easy" : chance==2 ? "Easier" : "Simple");
      if speed_class != 3: text(" "); text(speed_class>=6 ? "VVSlow" : speed_class==5 ? "V Slow"
          : speed_class==4 ? "Slow" : speed_class==2 ? "Fast" : speed_class<=1 ? "V Fast" : "");
      text(" strike, "); text(contact_quality(entry.contact));
      draw_independent_advantage_marks(entry.flags);
      // Stage 4 then draws quick/heavy/wild/precise, charge and multi-attack choices, not stage 5.
      if controlled_unit_is_enraged:
        text("No quick attack: enraged"); text("No heavy attack: enraged");
        text("Forced wild attack: enraged"); text("No precise attack: enraged");
      else:
        text("Quick attack: faster to strike and recover, but not powerful");
        text("Heavy attack: slower to strike and recover, but hits harder");
        text("Wild attack: fast strike, slow recovery, hard but unbalancing/inaccurate");
        text("Precise attack: very slow to strike, improved accuracy");
      charge_disabled_reason = first applicable native prerequisite:
        no target; you on ground; you mounted; you chained; you in uncontrolled flight;
        you on vehicle; you on projectile; you climbing; target on ground; target mounted;
        target chained; target in uncontrolled flight; target on vehicle; target on projectile;
        target climbing; target same position; target position inaccessible; target too far;
      if disabled: text("No charge attack: " + reason);
      else text("Charge attack: move toward your opponent");
      text("Multi-attack: choose another simultaneous action afterward");
      break;
    case 8: case 9:
      // Relationships carry two selected objects. Each object is either an item ID or a unit/body-part ID.
      if relationship refers to an item:
        title = (flags choose "Both holding ","Grabbed their ","Grabbed your ","Sharing ")
                + item_designation(relationship.item);
      else:
        draw controlled_unit identity on the left, opponent identity on right,
        with native body-part/grip artwork; the identities are independent captions.
      if native branch offers possession: text("Gain possession of " + item_designation(item));
      if native branch offers grab: text("Grab " + target_field + " with " + own_field);
      text("Wrestle using " + own_field);
      switch(move_enum) { // jump table 0x8800e0
        0: text("Lock " + target_field + " with " + own_field); break; // 0x87e598
        1: text("Choke " + target_field); break;                       // 0x87e853
        2: text("Take-down by " + target_field); break;                 // 0x87eabf
        3: text("Throw by " + target_field); break;                     // 0x87ed3c
        4: text("Pinch " + target_field); break;                        // 0x87efbc
        5: text("Gouge " + target_field); break;                        // 0x87f22f
        10: text("Break " + target_field); break;                       // 0x87f49f
        11:
          if relationship.owner_flag>0:
            prefix = grip_kind<=1 ? "Release grip of " : grip_kind==2 ? "Release joint lock of " : "Release choke of ";
            text(prefix + own_field + " on " + target_field);
          else:
            prefix = grip_kind<=1 ? "Break grip of " : grip_kind==2 ? "Loosen joint lock of " : "Loosen choke of ";
            text(prefix + target_field + " on " + own_field);
          break;                                                      // 0x87f721
        12: text("Shake " + target_field); break;                      // 0x87fa4b
        13: text("Strangle " + target_field); break;                   // 0x87fccc
        default: no caption; // native entries 6,7,8,9 and outside 0..13.
      }
      // own_field/target_field use c65450 for item IDs, otherwise 13345d0 for anatomy.
      break;
  }

contact_quality(q)
  q<=-3 -> "can only graze"; -2 -> "can't land squarely"; -1 -> "can't quite connect";
  0 -> "fairly solid"; 1 -> "square"; 2 -> "very square"; q>=3 -> "direct hit".

Dynamic fields and translation boundaries
  Unit name/role/species/curse/custom job follows 0x132e430 and 0x1331500 native getters;
  see helper-decompiled.txt and pre-existing ../adventure-unit-reference-sources.tsv.
  Body part follows 0x13345d0: selected RAW body-part name or exact fallback "body part".
  Item follows 0xc65450: complete native designation with optional " (copy)";
  vtable item naming/material and RAW attack names are dynamic authored game data.
  Rating follows 0x7737c0: exact 0..14 plus Legendary default, no skill names nor Legendary+N.
  Action/status follows 0x852640 over candidate.action_vector_0x7d0, including inline string copies.
  Full status enum/assembly, directions and summary coordinates are in helper-decompiled.txt.

The scoped runtime catalog adventure-target-translations.tsv retains:
  fixed literals, typed composite templates, source capture ordering, indexed Chinese targets,
  all rating and action-status enum texts, attack difficulty/contact/speed texts,
  direction/altitude/distance qualifiers, and all selectable wrestling captions.
  Punctuation and artwork comparison literals NO_SUB/stab/etc are retained in literal extraction.
  Dynamic human names, RAW species, materials, weapons, attack labels and anatomy are processed
  by their native getter translators rather than replacing arbitrary English substrings globally.

Additional geometry from renderer arithmetic
  Stage 2/5/6/7 list record top is T+13, records extend [top,top+3).
  Stage 3 record top is T+4, records extend [top,top+3).
  Stage 4 record top is T+4; content list ends at B-19 to reserve style controls below.
  Stage 8/9 relation count C=len(screen+0x128)+len(screen+0x140).
    relation divider D = C==0 ? T+2 : C<5 ? (T+2)+1+3*C : (T+2)+16.
    relation records begin T+4, have pitch 3, and show at most 5 relationships.
    move records begin D+2 and also have pitch 3; text baseline is recordTop+1.
  NO_SUB is compared as a missing RAW subtype sentinel; that subtype is not appended.
  It is not a visible "unknown" caption and is absent from the runtime translation table.

Native owner, layer writes and exact control geometry (additional reverse-engineered source)
  reference vtable viewscreen_dungeonmodest = 0x16b9f48;
  vtable slot +24 is render() at 0x7f3cb0 (pointer stored at RVA 0x16b9f60).
  render() calls adventure global UI renderer 0xaf1190 at 0x7f3dba,0x7f3e0c,0x7f3e73.
  That renderer owns the sole direct call to AttackCreature::render():
    0xb03469: if (*(byte*)(base+0x18a8728)) {
    0xb03472:   R9d = local right/map coordinate;
    0xb03476:   R8d = local bottom/map coordinate;
    0xb0347a:   EDX = *(int*)(base+0x23ca688);
    0xb03480:   RCX = base+0x18a8728; // global AttackCreature UI state
    0xb03487:   call 0x878600;
               }
  The combat panel therefore belongs to viewscreen_dungeonmodest and does not
  introduce a child viewscreen. A screen-type gate accepting current dungeonmodest
  accepts this native renderer. Full caller assembly is retained in
  helper-reference-dungeon-render.asm and helper-reference-adventure-global-render.asm.

  graphicst reference base is RVA 0x264a3f0. Texture matrices are column-major [column][row]:
    +0x1924..0x1944 hover_rectangle; main outer frame at 0x8786b3..0x878774.
    +0x19a8..0x19c8 button_rectangle; root action record at 0x879590..0x879696.
    +0xa768..0xa788 button_horizontal_option_active; stage-1 Confirm.
    +0xa7e0..0xa800 button_horizontal_option_remove; stage-1 Cancel.
    +0xa804..0xa824 button_horizontal_option_confirm; non-stage-1 Done.
  Stage-1 Confirm: inclusive outer [L+2,L+12] x [B-3,B-1], width11,height3.
    Caption L+4,B-2; hotkey L+4,B-1.
  Stage-1 Cancel: inclusive outer [R-11,R-2] x [B-3,B-1], width10,height3.
    Caption R-9,B-2; hotkey R-9,B-1.
  Stage-1 deliberately omits Done (0x878781..0x878786).
  Root stage2/5/6/7 action records have native outer x=[L+1,R-1], shortened to
  [L+1,R-3] only when a scrollbar is required; rowTop=T+13+3*visible_index.
    0x879502 rowTop = (T+2)+11.
    0x879562 textY = rowTop+1.
    0x87969a key at L+1,textY.
    0x8796d1 caption at L+3,textY.
    0x879ef6 textY += 3.
  The matrix draw always uses button_rectangle, not type_filter.
  Ratings are generated as one caption such as "Dodge (" + rating + ")" and
  emitted once at 0x879ef1 through text draw 0xad9960. The native parentheses
  remain characters of this caption; this renderer draws no separate slider,
  type-filter left/right arrows or rating text-strip skin.

  draw_lower_tile(gps,packed) at [0xadaad0,0xadac1c):
    if cursor outside gps clip rectangle: return;
    index = cursor_x*gps.dimy + cursor_y;
    if init.display.flags[0]&USE_GRAPHICS:
      gps.screentexpos_lower[index] = packed;
    else:
      screen[index].char = packed & 255;
      screen[index].fgRGB = palette[((packed>>8)&7) + 8*((packed>>14)&1)];
      screen[index].bgRGB = palette[(packed>>11)&7];
      gps.screentexpos[index] = 0;
    // Neither branch clears screentexpos_lower; no anchored buffer is written.

  draw_text(gps,string,mode,cap) at [0xad9960,0xad9a33):
    convert native string to character bytes via 0x6f5d0;
    if cap != 0 and converted.size>cap: truncate via 0x52d910;
    foreach visible byte until configured display width:
      draw_character(gps,byte,advance=1); // 0xad9a00 -> 0xbb190
  draw_character at [0xbb190,0xbb33c):
    if cursor inside clip and screen range:
      write screen character and foreground/background RGB from current gps;
      gps.screentexpos[index]=0; // 0xbb31c..0xbb323
    cursor_x += advance;
    // Does not clear/write screentexpos_lower or anchored buffers in either mode.

  draw_anchored_tile_rectangle(gps,tile,anchorX,anchorY,width,height,modulate)
    at [0xadad70,0xadb092):
    foreach clipped cell in [cursor_x,cursor_x+width) x [cursor_y,cursor_y+height):
      gps.screentexpos_anchored[index] = tile;     // gps+0x200
      gps.screentexpos_anchored_x[index] = anchorX; // gps+0x208
      gps.screentexpos_anchored_y[index] = anchorY; // gps+0x210
      if first cell: gps.screentexpos_flag[index] &= ~4;
      else: gps.screentexpos_flag[index] = 4 | ((dx<=63?dx:0)<<6) | ((dy<=63?dy:0)<<12);
      if modulate:
        write current foreground/background RGB to screen[index];
        gps.screentexpos_flag[index] |= 0x20;
      else: gps.screentexpos_flag[index] &= ~0x20;
    // No screen glyph write. No screentexpos_lower/primary write or clear.
  Native summary portrait call 0x873145 passes width12,height8,modulate=false.
  The fallback miniature at 0x87325a passes width5,height3,modulate=false.
  Thus both text and portraits preserve graphical lower-layer summary/frame skins.
  In classic mode text replaces screen foreground/character and background with
  current gps text colors; it does not preserve those particular screen bytes.

  Equivalent classic layer routines extracted from the configured official PE:
    text draw [0xad69a0,0xad6a73); character draw [0xbb190,0xbb33c);
    anchored portrait [0xad7db0,0xad80d2); lower tile [0xad7b10,0xad7c5c).
  Their full machine code is retained in helper-classic-*-draw.asm and
  helper-classic-*-tile.asm, and paired ranges in helper-edition-function-ranges.tsv.

Complete authored dynamic display leaves (additional source extraction)
  helper-reference-raw-display-fields.tsv and helper-classic-raw-display-fields.tsv
  retain both configured installations' vanilla and installed_mods object fields,
  including BODY BP, INDIVIDUAL_NAME/BP_NAME variants, all creature/caste/juvenile
  identity names, weapon/tool/natural attack names, item nouns/adjectives and
  material state names/adjectives/prefixes. The source rows retain RAW owners,
  caste/material context, exact file/line and the native expanded field.
  STP expands to that token's singular name; NO_SUB is omitted by native code.
  helper-raw-display-productions.tsv retains the native Lua source expressions
  that create these fields, without executing procedural generation.
  Runtime authored nicknames, generated history/procedural names and mod/save
  content remain semantic getter fields; no finite fixed English list describes
  them. Material/item naming uses the shared item-description source catalogs
  item-description-sources.tsv, item-raw-title-sources.tsv, corpse-caption-sources.tsv
  and the virtual/RAW formatter dependencies recorded in helper-decompiled.txt.

Stage 3 and 4 selectable record geometry from native renderer operands
  Both stages use inclusive outer record x=[L+1,E], E=R-1 ordinarily and
  E=R-3 when the scrollbar shortens records. Record pitch is three text rows.
  The attack/bodypart icon occupies [L+1,L+5) across three rows; key is at L+5.
  Dot/name begins at L+7 with a 36-character native cap. Name and statistics
  are both at recordTop+1; statistics begin at L+45. Native + and - markers
  occupy E-2, while ! occupies E-1; these fields have independent native draws.
